title: Pond ecology, fish and plant balance
audience: Pond and water-feature maintenance technicians and gardeners who service ponds with fish, plants and wildlife
learningOutcomes: Describe the producers, consumers and decomposers in a garden pond and explain how they depend on one another
Identify common causes of imbalance, including overfeeding, organic debris, nutrient runoff, low oxygen and pump failure
Choose a first response to stressed fish that checks the pump, aeration and temperature before any other action
Keep pool chemicals and other non-pond products out of a pond with fish or plants, and refer any request the owner's plan does not cover

instruction.heading: A pond is a living system
instruction.body: A garden pond is a small ecosystem in which water, plants, animals and microorganisms depend on one another. Producers are the plants that make food from light and dissolved nutrients: submerged plants, floating plants, plants with floating leaves, and the microscopic algae (phytoplankton) that float in open water and can colour it green. Consumers feed on other living things. Small grazing animals such as snails, insects and tadpoles eat algae and plant matter, fish and frogs eat those animals, and birds and turtles sit higher in the food web. Decomposers, mainly bacteria and fungi in the sediment and the filter, break down dead material and return nutrients to the plants. Because each group relies on the others, a problem in one part, such as too much food, shows up in the water quality and in the health of the fish. A pond with clean water, some shade, a range of plants and varied habitats supports the widest range of wildlife, and a balanced pond tends to need less intervention.

instruction.heading: Common causes of imbalance
instruction.body: Overfeeding is one of the most common causes of poor water. Uneaten food and fish waste add nutrients, feed algae and, as they decompose, use up dissolved oxygen. Leaves, needles and other organic debris add to the same load, and they are hardest to remove once they have started to rot. Nutrients also enter ponds from outside. Fertiliser and other pollutants carried by runoff from lawns and paved areas can reach a pond directly or through the stormwater system, and nutrient-rich water encourages rapid algae growth. When algae die, more organic matter builds up and the cycle speeds up. Warm, still weather lowers the oxygen the water can hold, and warm water also speeds up decay. A stopped pump or a clogged filter removes both mechanical filtration and aeration. Shade is not always a problem. In natural settings, shade and leaf litter combined with clean water support habitats that open, sunlit ponds may not, so cutting back trees is an owner decision with ecological effects, not a routine maintenance step.

instruction.heading: First response to stressed fish
instruction.body: When fish gasp at the surface, act on the most likely immediate cause first, which is usually low oxygen. Check that the pump is running and that any aeration is working. Measure the water temperature in degrees Celsius and record the time. Check the feeding record and remove uneaten food. If the water is clearly poor, a small partial water change with conditioned water at a similar temperature may help, but it must follow the owner's plan and be gradual. Do not add a chemical to force a result. Record what you found and what you did. If fish are dying in numbers, or an odour or cloudiness stays after these steps, stop the adjustments and refer the matter to the owner and, where appropriate, to a qualified aquatic specialist.

instruction.heading: Cleaning and water changes
instruction.body: Clean the pond gradually. Remove excess debris by hand or with a net, and do not remove all the sediment or all the plants in one session. The bacteria in the filter and the sediment, and the plants, keep the system stable, and a complete clean removes them together, which can cause a sudden fall in water quality. Partial water changes should be modest. Condition tap water to remove chlorine and chloramine before it enters the pond, and match its temperature to the pond as closely as is practical. Sudden changes in temperature or water chemistry are a common cause of fish stress, and a sudden large change should be avoided even when the water looks poor.

instruction.heading: Keeping non-pond products out
instruction.body: Pool chlorine, pool algaecides, pool pH products and other pool chemicals are formulated for a different system and must not be used in a pond with fish or plants. Pond treatment products are chosen for the specific system and are used only where the owner's instruction and the product label allow them. Read the label and the safety data sheet before any product is used. Storage needs care as well. So keep pond products separate from pool chemicals, out of reach of children and pets, and away from anything that could mix with them. Chemical control of pests, weeds or fish is not taught in this course. Those tasks need product-label checks, state rules and, where a licence applies, the licence, and they sit outside this lesson.

instruction.heading: When to refer, and moving fish
instruction.body: Refer to the owner when fish die in numbers, when an odour or cloudiness does not respond to the usual steps, when disease is suspected, or when a treatment is requested that is not in the owner's instruction. Moving live fish is regulated. In Western Australia, the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development says that moving live fish within the state needs a translocation approval. Queensland and New South Wales rules on restricted fish, releases and sightings are set out in the water-movement lesson (“Water conservation and environmental release for ponds”).

procedure: Check the pump and any aeration first when fish are stressed or the water is poor, and restore them before any other action.
Measure the water temperature in degrees Celsius and record it with the time.
Check the feeding record and remove uneaten food and excess debris.
Remove debris gradually; do not clean all sediment or all plants in one session.
If a partial water change is in the owner's plan, use conditioned water at a similar temperature and record the volume.
Do not add pool chemicals or any product that is not approved for the pond and in the owner's instruction.
Refer and record any mortality, unusual odour, cloudiness that persists, or suspected disease.

workedExamples.situation: A client's pond fish are gasping at the surface on a hot afternoon, and the pump has stopped since the morning.
workedExamples.reasoning: Low oxygen from the stopped pump is the most likely immediate cause. The technician restores the pump and any aeration, measures the water temperature in Celsius, checks the feeding record and removes uneaten food. A partial water change with conditioned water at a similar temperature is made only if the owner's plan allows it and the water is clearly poor. No pool chemical is added. The event, the readings and the response are recorded, and any fish deaths are referred to the owner.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks for a cup of pool chlorine to clear green water quickly before a party.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you tell the client?
workedExamples.reasoning: Pool chlorine is not used in a pond with fish and plants. The technician declines, explains that it can harm fish, plants and the bacteria that keep the pond stable, and records the request and the refusal. The technician then offers to check the pump, filter, feeding and debris, and to recommend only a product for the pond where the label and the owner's instruction allow it.

equipmentAndPpe: Thermometer for water temperature in degrees Celsius
Water test kit suited to ponds, with reagents in date
Water conditioner suited to the pond, in date, used as the label directs

commonErrors.error: Adding pool chlorine or pool algaecide to a pond.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only products approved for the pond and only with the owner's instruction and the label.

commonErrors.error: Removing all plants or all sediment in one session.
commonErrors.prevention: Clean gradually to keep the bacteria and plants that stabilise the pond.

commonErrors.error: Overfeeding, or leaving uneaten food in the water.
commonErrors.prevention: Feed according to the owner's plan, and remove uneaten food and the debris it creates.

commonErrors.error: Adding chemicals to a stressed pond before checking the pump and aeration.
commonErrors.prevention: Restore pump and aeration first, measure the temperature, then decide on the next step.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Pool chemicals and pond treatment products must be stored and used separately. Read the label and the safety data sheet for each product, and keep products away from children and pets.
In Western Australia, moving live fish needs a translocation approval.

This lesson does not authorise fish movement, release, medication, or chemical control of pests, weeds or fish. Those activities need product-label checks, state rules and any licence that applies. Completing this lesson does not grant any of them.
Pool water chemistry rules apply to pools and spas. They do not set the care of a pond, which is set by the owner's plan and the product labels.

qualityStandard: Pump and aeration are checked before any other action when fish are stressed
No pool chemical or non-approved product is added to the pond
Cleaning and water changes are gradual and recorded with volumes and temperatures
documentationEvidence: Visit record with water temperature in Celsius, feeding and pump status
Water change volume, conditioner used and the owner's approval
Mortality, odour or disease report and the referral made to the owner
summary: A pond is a living system of producers, consumers and decomposers, and most problems come from too much food or debris, low oxygen or a stopped pump.
Restore pump and aeration first when fish are stressed, then measure, record and decide.
Clean and change water gradually to protect the bacteria and plants.
Never add pool chemicals to a pond with fish or plants, and refer what the owner's plan does not cover.

knowledgeChecks.question: A pond has fish gasping at the surface on a hot day and the pump has stopped. What is the first response?
options: Add pool chlorine to clean the water quickly, since it will clear it fast
Remove all the plants at once, since they are using up the oxygen
Overfeed the fish to help them recover, since the food will give them energy
Restore pump and aeration, then check temperature and water results

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a pond not be cleaned of all sediment and all plants at once?
options: It removes the bacteria and plants that help keep the system stable
It makes the fish happy and more active during the warm months
It adds oxygen to the water and helps the pump run better
It is required by law for every pond in the state and council

knowledgeChecks.question: Which product is correct for a pond with fish and plants?
options: Pool chlorine in a small dose, since it is only a little for the pond
A pond-approved product used under the owner's instruction and the label
Any pool algaecide, since it is the same as the pond product
Bleach from the laundry, diluted in a bucket of pond water first
